_comment: Medical REVIEW PROCESS steps for the prototype: who looks at what, and how the review is recorded. These are workflow settings, NOT clinical protocols: they contain no diagnoses, treatments, medications or clinical thresholds. A real deployment must replace them with the mission's approved medical operations procedures.

critical.label: Escalate now to qualified medical personnel
critical.why: A critical-severity alert, or concurrent deviations across systems, can indicate a potentially serious situation that software must not assess on its own.

caution.label: Request flight-surgeon review
caution.why: A caution-severity alert needs review by qualified medical personnel.

advisory.label: Include in the routine medical review
advisory.who: Mission operator, then the flight surgeon at the next routine review
advisory.why: Advisory alerts are informational unless they persist or recur.

steps.label: Notify the reviewer named in the escalation level
Check whether a simulated test scenario explains the alert (shown under environmental context)
Check signal quality: data completeness, gaps and sensor status listed under data quality
Review activity at the time, the baseline comparison and concurrent deviations in other systems
Flight surgeon reviews the measurements and decides on any follow-up under the mission's own medical procedures
Record the review outcome in an incident report (review status and reviewer note)
Acknowledge or resolve the alert in ASTRA-MED once reviewed
